subject: POC kickoff: workload intake, evaluation playbook & next steps
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Mary Thompson <mary@olivetech.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: POC kickoff: workload intake, evaluation playbook & next steps

Hi Mary,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — good conversation. As promised, here’s a concise post-call recap and an ask to help us stand up the POC quickly. Goal: validate performance and cost for your production traffic shape, confirm any functional/regulatory constraints, and agree on success criteria so we can hand off to engineering.

1) High-level success criteria (proposed)
- p50 latency for user-facing generative endpoints < 250 ms (hosted) / < 200 ms (dedicated)
- Sustained throughput to meet 95th percentile of your production RPS with <0.1% error rate
- Model output parity on our eval prompt set: >= 95% pass rate on critical prompts

2) Suggested evaluation plan (phases)
- Phase A: traffic intake & baseline (1 week) — we ingest representative sample, run baseline on hosted SKU
- Phase B: capacity simulation (1 week) — run target concurrency/peak bursts against dedicated-like profiles
- Phase C: stability & regression checks (1 week) — continuous run with monitoring & quality checks

3) What we need from you (by next Tue, 10/19)
- Sample traffic extract (anonymized) or a 24–48h synthetic sample that matches peak bursts
- RPS expectations: steady-state, peak, and typical burst duration (seconds/minutes)
- Token length distributions (avg prompt tokens / avg response tokens / 95th pct)
- Concurrency expectations and client-side retry/backoff behavior
- Any payload size limits, attachments, or streaming requirements
- Security/compliance constraints (EU-only data, IP allowlists, mutual TLS, etc.)

Attached: poc_workload_template.xlsx and traffic_sample.jsonl (example format). Please drop your sample to the Drive link above or reply with a sample attached — if you prefer SFTP we can provide a one-time dropbox.

Proposed kickoff: Wed 10/14 between 9–11am CET or Thu 10/15 2–3pm CET. Please confirm what works for you.

Owners on our side: Evelyn (sales, overall POC coordination), Lauren (CS lead / evaluation criteria), Rishi (SRE runtime & performance), Dev (infrastructure liaison).

Next step: Mary — can you confirm sample delivery and which region you want the trial in (you mentioned EU during the call)? Also confirm any procurement or NDA steps we should be aware of.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
E: evelyn_hart@redwood.com | M: (415) 555-0187

Attachments: poc_workload_template.xlsx (spreadsheet), traffic_sample.jsonl (example)
From: Mary Thompson <mary@olivetech.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: James Wu <james@olivetech.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T12:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff: workload intake, evaluation playbook & next steps

Evelyn, thanks — that recap is great and aligned with our goals. Quick answers below and I attached a small sample.

- Region: EU (data residency required for user text and logs)
- Steady-state RPS: ~80 requests/sec
- Expected peak RPS (short bursts): ~420 rps for bursts lasting ~2–4 minutes, maybe once or twice per hour during high-traffic windows
- Concurrency: typical concurrency ~40, peak concurrency ~120
- Token lengths: avg prompt ~40 tokens, avg response ~160 tokens, 95th pct response ~450 tokens
- Typical retry behavior: client retries once after 1500ms, exponential backoff thereafter
- Payloads: sometimes include base64-encoded attachments; max payload size ~1.5MB

Attached: olive_traffic_sample.jsonl (anonymized lines). Procurement: we have a PO number in process (OLV-PO-421) — procurement will follow after we agree on scope and length of trial.

We can do kickoff Thu 10/15 2pm CET — James and I will join. We’d prefer the POC run as hosted EU endpoints first, then evaluate dedicated capacity.

Thanks,
Mary Thompson
Head of Product | Olive Tech
mary@olivetech.com

Attachments: olive_traffic_sample.jsonl

Thanks Mary / Evelyn — good detail. Looping in implementation owners and listing a few clarifying items before the Thu kickoff: 

- Rishi: can you confirm whether EU-hosted default runtime will meet the p50/p95 latency targets for the stated token sizes and bursts? Also: are we good with KV cache warmup strategy for short 2–4 minute bursts?
- Dev: please prepare an intake runbook (we'll attach eu-region-constraints.md) and a temp S3/GCS drop location for Olive's sample if they prefer not to use Drive.
- Evelyn: I’ll own the evaluation criteria doc and the pass/fail prompt set. I’ll circulate the initial draft by tomorrow EOD.

Mary — we may have a couple of follow-ups in the kickoff focused on: authentication options (API key vs mTLS), max connections per IP, and log retention for EU trials.

Proposed technical kickoff link: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=olive-poc-kickoff-20261015 (tentative). I attached eu-region-constraints.md covering data residency notes and minimal onboarding checklist.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
